actions.mechanism: Separate presence from condition so counting cannot imply inspection or verified good condition.
actions.implementation: Create ten ID-labelled rows on a shared form: presence, condition category or unknown, inspector, and inspection time. Default condition to unknown.
actions.check: Record ten present components without inspecting condition; all ten must remain unknown, with no verified-good summary.
actions.risk: Default selections must not silently populate inspection evidence.

actions.mechanism: Separate responsibility for follow-up from authorship of inspection evidence.
actions.implementation: Record outgoing staff, incoming staff, transfer time, and unresolved component IDs. Incoming staff acknowledge ownership without changing inspector fields; absent acknowledgment, the shift lead owns follow-up.
actions.check: Transfer a partially inspected kit; verify the next owner can identify unresolved IDs and original inspectors without verbal context.
actions.risk: Acknowledgment must not be presented as certification of condition.

actions.action: Open an owned task for every missing component
actions.mechanism: Turn missing status into a tracked obligation rather than a passive warning.
actions.implementation: For each missing ID, require a staff owner, next action, and due time; default to checking the kit’s storage location before contacting the borrower.
actions.check: Mark one component missing and change shifts; its task must retain an owner, deadline, and actionable instruction until explicitly resolved.
actions.risk: Missing status alone must not establish borrower fault.

actions.action: Timebox handoff and defer unfinished inspection explicitly
actions.mechanism: Preserve uncertainty when the three-minute limit prevents inspection completion.
actions.implementation: Use a desk clock: stop inspection at 150 seconds and reserve 30 seconds for ownership transfer. Queue remaining unknown IDs with an owner and deadline.
actions.check: Rehearse a ten-component return counted but not condition-checked: finish handoff within 180 seconds, preserving ten unknown conditions and owned follow-up.
actions.risk: Deferred checks can accumulate; the shift lead reviews overdue work.

actions.action: Separate return receipt from readiness to lend
actions.mechanism: Acknowledge custody without falsely certifying that a returned kit is ready for reuse.
actions.implementation: Provide distinct statuses: returned, inspection pending, and ready. Require all ten IDs present and checked against approved condition categories before marking ready.
actions.check: Accept a counted-only return; it must show returned and inspection pending, never ready, until component-level checks satisfy the rule.
actions.risk: Holding uninspected kits may temporarily reduce lending availability.

actions.action: Match components against an ID-labelled layout
actions.mechanism: A fixed ten-position layout exposes omissions and substitutions that an aggregate count can conceal.
actions.implementation: Print a reusable ID layout beside the handoff desk. Match visible component IDs to positions while recording presence; record condition separately.
actions.check: Present ten items including one duplicate and one absent expected ID; staff must record the absent ID rather than accept the count.
actions.risk: Layout placement is not evidence of condition inspection.

actions.action: Preserve corrections and reset evidence each loan
actions.mechanism: An append-only history prevents disputed edits and old inspections from masquerading as current evidence.
actions.implementation: Start each lending cycle with unknown return conditions. Retain prior records; append corrections with component ID, author, time, reason, and superseded value.
actions.check: Correct a good-condition entry to damaged, then start another loan; both historical entries remain readable and new return conditions start unknown.
actions.risk: The current value must remain obvious beside its history.
